## View an object

`cellucid_view()` opens a Seurat, SingleCellExperiment or SummarizedExperiment
object in the Cellucid viewer: in the RStudio or Positron Viewer pane, in
your browser, or, in a Jupyter notebook (IRkernel), in the cell's output.
Nothing is written to disk.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(cellucid)
library(SeuratObject)
data("pbmc_small")

viewer <- cellucid_view(pbmc_small)
```

The object is read as `cellucid_prepare(data = pbmc_small)` reads it -- cell
metadata, every reduction as `X_<name>`, the assays, the SNN graph -- into the
same Cellucid-ready AnnData, held in memory and uncompressed (the browser
reads it over loopback): only what the viewer asks for is made, when it asks,
and an object's genes x cells matrix is never transposed whole. Several assays (RNA and ADT, say) open as modalities,
with a Modality choice in the viewer's Data mapping.

The viewer is yours to talk to:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
cellucid_color_by(viewer, "groups")
cellucid_highlight(viewer, colnames(pbmc_small)[1:20], color = "#377eb8")

cellucid_on(viewer, "selection", function(event) {
  message(length(event$cells), " cells selected")
})
# ... select cells in the viewer with the lasso, then:
selected <- cellucid_selection(viewer)
subset(pbmc_small, cells = selected$cell_names)

# Every highlight group, label field, score and gene set made in the viewer,
# as meta.data columns (and misc$cellucid$gene_sets), in one call:
pbmc_small <- cellucid_pull(pbmc_small, viewer)
# A column of yours, shown in the viewer as a field:
cellucid_push(viewer, pbmc_small$RNA_snn_res.1, key = "clusters")
cellucid_stop(viewer)
```

The R console stays usable while the viewer is open: the server answers the
viewer whenever R is idle. Without a viewer, `cellucid_pull()` reads what the
web app exports (obs-column CSV files, GMT gene sets, `.cellucid-session`
files): `cellucid_pull(pbmc_small, "~/Downloads/cellucid-exports")`.

## In a Jupyter notebook

In an IRkernel notebook (JupyterLab, Notebook 7, VS Code, Google Colab's R
runtime) the same `cellucid_view(pbmc_small)` shows the viewer in the cell's
output: a notebook widget, the one cellucid-python's `show_anndata()` shows,
reached through the notebook's own connection, so no port or server is
involved. It needs the `IRkernel` and `IRdisplay` packages, and the Python
package `anywidget` where the notebook server runs. R hears the viewer
between cells: show the viewer in one cell, work in it, and call
`cellucid_pull()` or `cellucid_selection()` in the next. Runnable notebooks,
each with a Python twin and an "Open in Colab" badge:
<https://docs.cellucid.com/en/latest/user_guide/r_package/f_notebooks_tutorials/index.html>.

## Serve from a cluster

On a machine without a screen, `cellucid_serve()` serves the same viewer and
prints its address; reach it through an SSH tunnel:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
viewer <- cellucid_serve(sce)
#> Serving sce at http://127.0.0.1:8765
#> Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/?viewer=true&viewerId=...&viewerToken=...&anndata=true in a browser (from another machine: ssh -L 8765:127.0.0.1:8765 <this host>, then open the address there).
#> Stop it with cellucid_stop().
```

Port 8765 is the default because Google sign-in (community annotation) accepts
only that local address; when it is taken, the next free port is used and the
message says so. Behind RStudio Server or Posit Workbench, name the proxy's
host with `allowed_hosts = "rstudio.example.org"`.

## What the viewer reads

The web app itself is downloaded once, at first use, from www.cellucid.com
into `file.path(tools::R_user_dir("cellucid", "cache"), "web")`, and every file is checked
against the build's SHA-256 inventory before it is served.
`cellucid_clear_web_cache()` removes it.

The data side can be shown here without a browser: serve a store with
`serve_web_ui = FALSE` and ask the server what a viewer would ask. Because R
serves and asks in one process here, `fetch()` turns R's event loop while it
waits for the answer.

```{r}
library(cellucid)

store <- cellucid_prepare(
  file.path(tempdir(), "viewer-example.zarr"), "zarr",
  embeddings = list(X_umap = matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1), ncol = 2)),
  obs = data.frame(cluster = factor(c("a", "a", "b", "b"))),
  dataset_id = "viewer-example", dataset_name = "Viewer example",
  force = TRUE
)

viewer <- cellucid_serve(store, port = 0L, serve_web_ui = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
viewer

fetch <- function(path) {
  answer <- NULL
  pool <- curl::new_pool()
  curl::curl_fetch_multi(
    paste0(viewer$url, path), pool = pool,
    done = function(response) answer <<- response,
    fail = function(message) stop(message)
  )
  while (is.null(answer)) {
    curl::multi_run(timeout = 0, poll = TRUE, pool = pool)
    later::run_now(0.01)
  }
  rawToChar(answer$content)
}

cat(fetch("/_cellucid/datasets"))
cat(fetch("/_cellucid/anndata/viewer-example.zarr/obs/.zattrs"))

cellucid_stop(viewer)
```

The browser opens `_cellucid/datasets`, then reads the store key by key with
range requests, exactly as it reads a Cellucid-ready AnnData on any web host.
A file given by path (an `.h5ad`, a `.zarr.zip`, a Loom or 10x `.h5`, an
`.rds`) is served from disk as it is; the browser reads it itself.
